task_metadata.research_topic: diffusion model prediction parameterization for unconditional image generation
task_metadata.research_question: Can we design a prediction parameterization that achieves better FID than standard epsilon-, v-, and x0-prediction for CIFAR-10 diffusion training under a fixed compute budget?
notes: The task description explicitly frames epsilon prediction as Ho et al. (2020) and v-prediction as Salimans and Ho (2022).

The x0 baseline is linked approximately to later explicit data-prediction/preconditioning literature because this task uses direct x0 prediction as a parameterization rather than introducing a new named method.

tests.label: train_small
tests.notes: Small-scale CIFAR-10 diffusion training with a UNet backbone, DDIM sampling, AdamW optimization, and FID/clean-fid evaluation.

tests.label: train_medium
tests.notes: Medium-scale version of the same evaluation stack; the model width changes but the literature grounding is unchanged.

tests.label: train_large
tests.notes: Largest-capacity variant of the same DDPM-style UNet training setup and DDIM/FID evaluation protocol.

baselines.name: epsilon
baselines.notes: Matches the epsilon/noise-prediction parameterization described in the task and introduced in DDPM.

baselines.name: vpred
baselines.notes: Matches the velocity parameterization explicitly attributed to Salimans and Ho (2022) in the task description.

baselines.name: x0pred
baselines.notes: Direct x0/data prediction is a standard diffusion parameterization, but this link is approximate because the task baseline is not tied to a single named originating paper.

papers.title: Deep Unsupervised Learning using Nonequilibrium Thermodynamics
papers.relevance: Foundational diffusion-model paper that motivates the forward noising and learned reverse process used by later DDPM-style training.

papers.title: U-Net: Convolutional Networks for Biomedical Image Segmentation
papers.relevance: The task trains a UNet2DModel backbone, so the original U-Net paper is the canonical architecture reference.

papers.title: Decoupled Weight Decay Regularization
papers.relevance: The evaluation protocol explicitly uses AdamW, so this is the optimizer reference for all three tests.

papers.title: GANs Trained by a Two Time-Scale Update Rule Converge to a Local Nash Equilibrium
papers.relevance: Introduces Fréchet Inception Distance, the primary metric optimized by this task.

papers.title: Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models
papers.relevance: Primary paper for epsilon prediction and the DDPM-style CIFAR-10 training setup used by the task.

papers.title: Denoising Diffusion Implicit Models
papers.relevance: The task evaluates with a 50-step DDIM sampler, making DDIM the direct inference-time benchmark reference.

papers.title: Score-Based Generative Modeling through Stochastic Differential Equations
papers.relevance: Broadens the score-based interpretation of diffusion training and is relevant background for alternative parameterizations and samplers.

papers.title: Improved Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models
papers.relevance: Important follow-on DDPM paper covering learned variances and compute-quality tradeoffs relevant to fixed-budget CIFAR-10 diffusion evaluation.

papers.title: On Aliased Resizing and Surprising Subtleties in GAN Evaluation
papers.relevance: This is the clean-fid reference, directly matching the task's stated FID evaluation implementation.

papers.title: Progressive Distillation for Fast Sampling of Diffusion Models
papers.relevance: Introduces the v-parameterization explicitly referenced by the task description for the vpred baseline.

papers.title: Elucidating the Design Space of Diffusion-Based Generative Models
papers.relevance: Relevant explicit discussion of data/x0 prediction and diffusion preconditioning, used here as the closest literature anchor for the x0pred baseline.
